title: February 13–24 - 42nd Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 42nd annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 13 to 24 February 1992. The festival opened with The Inner Circle by Andrei Konchalovsky.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1992
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 1992 with the song "Träume sind für alle da", composed by Ralph Siegel, with lyrics by Bernd Meinunger, and performed by the band Wind. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk, selected their entry through a national final.
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1992

title: The 5.3 Mw Roermond earthquake affects Netherlands, Germany, and Belgium with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VII (Very strong).
text: The Modified Mercalli intensity scale measures the effects of an earthquake at a given location. This is in contrast with the seismic magnitude usually reported for an earthquake.

title: June 13-September 20: Documenta 9
text: DOCUMENTA IX was the ninth edition of documenta, a quinquennial contemporary art exhibition. It was held between 13 June and 20 September 1992 in Kassel, Germany.

title: July 6–8: The 18th G7 summit is held in Munich.
text: The 18th G7 Summit was held in Munich, Germany between 6 and 8 July 1992. The venue for the summit meetings was at the Residenz palace in central Munich.

title: August 22–24: Rostock-Lichtenhagen riots.
text: Violent xenophobic riots took place in the Lichtenhagen district of Rostock, Germany, from 22–24 August 1992. These were the worst mob attacks against migrants in postwar Germany.

title: The Mykonos restaurant assassinations occur in Berlin.
text: In the Mykonos restaurant assassinations, Iranian-Kurdish opposition leaders Sadegh Sharafkandi, Fattah Abdoli, Homayoun Ardalan and their translator Nouri Dehkordi, were assassinated at the Mykonos Greek restaurant in Berlin, Germany on 17 September 1992. The assassination took place during the KDPI insurgency (1989–96), as part of the general Kurdish separatism in Iran.

title: Tom & Jerry: The Movie is released to theaters.
text: Tom and Jerry: The Movie is a 1992 American animated musical comedy film based on the characters Tom and Jerry created by William Hanna and Joseph Barbera. It was produced and directed by Phil Roman, with a screenplay written by Dennis Marks, who also scripted some episodes of the then-airing TV series Tom & Jerry Kids.

title: Date unknown - The Scientology Task Force of the Hamburg Interior Authority is formed.
text: The Scientology Task Force of the Hamburg Interior Authority was founded in 1992 to monitor the activities and publications of Scientology, raise public awareness about the organization, and serve as a resource to Scientology members who may wish to exit the group. The Hamburg government made the decision to form the task force in 1991, after claiming in public statements that the Church of Scientology's aims incl…
wiki: Scientology Task Force of the Hamburg Interior Authority

title: 1991–92 ice hockey Bundesliga season
text: The 1991–92 ice hockey Bundesliga season was the 34th season of the Ice hockey Bundesliga, the top level of ice hockey in Germany. 12 teams participated in the league, and Düsseldorfer EG won the championship.

title: 1992 German motorcycle Grand Prix
text: The 1992 German motorcycle Grand Prix, held from the weekend of 12–14 June 1992, at the Hockenheim circuit was the seventh round of the 1992 Grand Prix motorcycle racing season.

title: Germany at the 1992 Summer Olympics
text: Germany competed at the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona, Spain. It was the first time the European nation participated in the Summer Games after German reunification in 1990 and for the first time as a single nation since 1936.

title: Germany at the 1992 Winter Olympics
text: Germany competed at the 1992 Winter Olympics in Albertville, France. It was the first time that the nation had competed at the Olympic Games following reunification in 1990 and for the first time as a single nation since 1936.

title: “Let's Talk About Sex” by Salt-n-Pepa
text: "Let's Talk About Sex" is a song by American hip hop trio Salt-N-Pepa, released in August 1991, by Next Plateau Records, as the fourth single from their third studio album, Blacks' Magic. It was written and co-produced by Hurby Azor, and achieved great success in many countries, including Australia, Austria, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Switzerland and Zimbabwe where it was a number-one hit.

title: “Das Boot” by 27 January
text: "Das Boot" is the title theme to the film and TV series Das Boot, composed and produced by Klaus Doldinger, and released as a single in 1981. In 1991, the song was covered by German DJ and producer Alex Christensen and his dance music project U96.

title: “To Be with You” by 27 April
text: "To Be with You" is a song by American rock band Mr. Big, released in November 1991 by Atlantic Records as the second single from their second album, Lean into It, on which it appears as the closing track.

title: “Rhythm Is a Dancer” by Snap!
text: "Rhythm Is a Dancer" is a song by German Eurodance group Snap!, released in March 1992 by Arista and Logic Records as the second single from their second studio album, The Madman's Return. It features vocals by American singer Thea Austin.

title: “It's My Life” by 3 August
text: "It's My Life" is a song by Nigerian-Swedish recording artist Dr. Alban.

title: “Sweat (A La La La La Long)” by 28 September
text: "Sweat" is a song by Jamaican reggae fusion band Inner Circle, released in July 1992 by Warner Bros. Records as the lead single from their twelfth album, Bad to the Bone (1992).
wiki: Sweat (A La La La La Long)
listen: Sweat (A La La La La Long) 28 September

title: “More and More” by 21 December
text: "More and More" is a song by German Eurodance music project Captain Hollywood Project. It was released in July 1992 by the record labels Blow Up and Dino Music as the first single from their first album, Love Is Not Sex.
wiki: More and More (Captain Hollywood Project song)

title: Asteroid 5751 Zao is discovered by Masahiro Koishikawa.
text: An asteroid is a minor planet that orbits within the inner Solar System or is co-orbital with Jupiter. These objects are larger than a meteoroid (thus 1 meter or larger) and are neither a planet nor an identified comet.

title: First confirmed detection of exoplanets with announcement of the discovery of several terrestrial-mass planets orbiting the pulsar PSR B1257+12 by radio astronomers Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail working in the United States.
text: An exoplanet or extrasolar planet is a planet outside the Solar System. The first confirmed detection of an exoplanet was in 1992 around a pulsar, and the first detection around a main-sequence star was in 1995.

title: Discovery of 15760 Albion, the first trans-Neptunian object to be found after Pluto and Charon.
text: 15760 Albion was the first trans-Neptunian object to be discovered after Pluto and Charon. Measuring about 108–167 kilometres in diameter, it was discovered in 1992 by David C. Jewitt and Jane X. Luu at the Mauna Kea Observatory, Hawaii.

title: Pope John Paul II issues an apology and lifts the 1633 edict of the Inquisition against Galileo Galilei.
text: Pope John Paul II was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 16 October 1978 until his death in 2005. He was the first non-Italian pope since Adrian VI in the 16th century, as well as the third longest-serving pope in history, after St.

title: The Goosebumps series of children's horror fiction, penned by R. L. Stine, is first published in the United States.
text: Robert Lawrence Stine is an American novelist. He is the writer of Goosebumps, a horror fiction novel series for children which has sold over 400 million copies globally in 35 languages, becoming the second-best-selling book series in history.

title: An attempt is made to set fire to the National Library of Abkhazia in Sukhumi during the War in Abkhazia by Georgian forces.
text: The War in Abkhazia was fought between Georgian government and paramilitary forces, and a coalition of Abkhaz separatist forces and North Caucasian militants between 1992 and 1993. Ethnic Georgians who lived in Abkhazia fought largely on the side of Georgian government forces.

title: The National and University Library of Bosnia and Herzegovina is annihilated during the Siege of Sarajevo by the Army of Republika Srpska.
text: The siege of Sarajevo was a prolonged military blockade of Sarajevo, the capital of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, during the ethnically charged Bosnian War. The city was initially besieged by the Yugoslav People's Army, before they were replaced by elements of the newly-formed Army of Republika Srpska.

title: Michael Ondaatje's historiographic metafiction The English Patient is published in Canada. It will win The Golden Man Booker in 2018.
text: Philip Michael Ondaatje is a Sri Lankan-born Canadian poet, fiction writer and essayist. Ondaatje's literary career began with his poetry: in 1967 he published The Dainty Monsters, and in 1970 the critically acclaimed The Collected Works of Billy the Kid.

title: British fashion designer Alexander McQueen shows his first collection, partly inspired by The Silence of the Lambs (film).
text: Lee Alexander McQueen was a British fashion designer and couturier. Known for his unconventional designs, he was one of the most influential fashion designers in the world from the early 1990s until his death by suicide in 2010.

title: Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum in Madrid is opened to the public as a gallery for the private art collection of the Thyssen-Bornemisza family.
text: The Thyssen-Bornemisza National Museum, or simply the Thyssen, is an art museum in Madrid, Spain, located near the Prado Museum on one of the city's main boulevards. It is known as part of the "Golden Triangle of Art", which also includes the Prado and the Reina Sofía national galleries.
